# geluTanh

> Evaluate the [Gaussian error linear unit][activation-function] (GELU) using a tanh approximation.

<section class="intro">

The [Gaussian error linear unit][activation-function] (GELU) using a tanh approximation is defined as:

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:gelu_tanh" align="center" raw="\mathrm{gelu}(x) \approx \frac{x}{2} \left[ 1 + \tanh\left( \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \left( x + 0.044715 \, x^3 \right) \right) \right]" alt="GELU tanh approximation."> -->

```math
\mathrm{gelu}(x) \approx \frac{x}{2} \left[ 1 + \tanh\left( \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \left( x + 0.044715 \, x^3 \right) \right) \right]
```

<!-- </equation> -->

where $\tanh(x)$ is the [hyperbolic tangent][hyperbolic-functions].

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var geluTanh = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/fast/gelu-tanh' );
```

#### geluTanh( x )

Evaluates the Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU) activation function using a tanh approximation.

```javascript
var v = geluTanh( 0.0 );
// returns 0.0

v = geluTanh( 1.0 );
// returns ~0.8412

v = geluTanh( -Infinity );
// returns -0.0

v = geluTanh( Infinity );
// returns Infinity

v = geluTanh( NaN );
// returns NaN
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var logEachMap = require( '@stdlib/console/log-each-map' );
var geluTanh = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/fast/gelu-tanh' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float64'
};
var x = uniform( 100, -5.0, 5.0, opts );

logEachMap( 'geluTanh(%0.4f) = %0.4f', x, geluTanh );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<!-- C usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/fast/gelu_tanh.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_fast_gelu_tanh( x )

Evaluates the Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU) activation function using a tanh approximation.

```c
double y = stdlib_base_fast_gelu_tanh( 1.0 );
// returns ~0.8412
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**: `[in] double` input value.

```c
double stdlib_base_fast_gelu_tanh( const double x );
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- C API usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/fast/gelu_tanh.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    const double x[] = { -5.0, -3.89, -2.78, -1.67, -0.56, 0.56, 1.67, 2.78, 3.89, 5.0 };

    double v;
    int i;
    for ( i = 0; i < 10; i++ ) {
        v = stdlib_base_fast_gelu_tanh( x[ i ] );
        printf( "gelu_tanh(%lf) = %lf\n", x[ i ], v );
    }
}
```

</section>
